_comment: Luke Rhodes voice-lint configuration. voice_lint.py reads this via --config; without it the script falls back to built-in defaults, which leaves the AU-spelling check, the stylometric fingerprint comparison, the exclamation/emoji rations and the repeat allowlist switched off. The predecessor package shipped no config and never passed --config, so those checks were dead code. Every entry below traces to a rule already stated in prose in luke-voice.md or a persona file; the config is the mechanical half of a rule the package already claimed to enforce.
_banned_phrases_note: Self-narrating meta-labels. luke-voice.md states the rule ('No self-narrating meta-labels ... A person being brief is simply brief; a label promising brevity or honesty is the tell') and SKILL.md claimed 'The lint bans the worst of these'. It did not: all four named examples passed clean before this file existed. These are hard failures because the rule is a hard rule.
advisory_phrases: so you can focus on what matters
_advisory_phrases_note: Announcement boilerplate. Advisory rather than hard-fail because a couple of these have legitimate uses in a genuinely celebratory line; the warning exists so the writer has to choose them on purpose.
_fingerprint_note: Computed with `voice_lint.py --extract-fingerprint references/corpus/luke-anchors.txt` over 480 words of verbatim Luke prose recovered from the sample anchors quoted across the package. The original my-voice.txt corpus was an input to the first build and was never committed, so 480 words is what survives. That is below the ~800-word workable floor and well below the ~2,000-word stability threshold in voice-replication-research.md: treat these numbers as rough, and read a fingerprint warning as a prompt to look rather than as a verdict. Recompute from a fuller corpus when one is available; the semicolon rate in particular rests on a handful of instances.
_repeat_allowlist_note: Domain nouns that repeat naturally in Luke's subject matter. Elegant variation is itself an AI tell, so a product name recurring is correct; the repeated-phrase check exists to catch a rhetorical phrase or a landing line recurring, not a term.
